text.p: These are the leading stories in the Turkish press on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Provincial heads of the ruling Islamist Welfare Party are going to Ankara to urge clear party support for religious schools threatened with closure. A top military board asks for the implementation of eight-year, uninterrupted education which would lead to the partial closure of these schools.
- Bureaucrats say Islamist Prime Minister Necmettin Erbakan is following an election-time economic policy.
- Two boats carrying Iraqi illegal immigrants to Greece sink in the Aegean Sea.
- Two pilots are sacked from Turkish Airlines for fighting on board a Turkey-Bangkok flight.
- A parliamentary commission is to resume discussion of a draft pension law vetoed by President Suleyman Demirel.
- Opposition parties present a motion to investigate an armed attack on the private television channel Flash TV.
- The monthly consumer price inflation rate falls in April from the year earlier level to 6.6 percent.
- Deputies from the conservative coalition partner are split over the implementation of an eight-year, uninterrupted compulsory education plan.
- A visit by Azerzbaijan President Haidar Aliyev to Turkey is the last chance for an oil pipeline project between Baku and Ceyhan in southern Turkey.
- Prime Minister Erbakan said the economy made considerable losses in March and April because of artificial agendas that led to a political crisis.
